**News:**4 days ago Penix completed 25 of 34 passes for 213 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions and added five carries for minus-1 yard in the Falcons' 29-20 win over the 49ers on Sunday. He also recovered a fumble.
**Spin:**Penix put together a solid, mistake-free effort that saw him toss a trio of touchdown passes for the second straight game. The 2024 first-round pick connected with Nick Muse (one yard), Kyle Pitts (five yards) and Drake London (21 yards) for his trio of scoring strikes, the latter two coming in the second half. Penix also completed over 71.0 percent of his passes for the third time in five games this season, and he'll take an excellent 9:1 TD:INT and 1,157 passing yards into a Week 8 road matchup against the Buccaneers next Sunday.
texts.4:
**ESPN Fantasy Projection:**Penix is no longer guaranteed a starting job entering his third season. The 2024 first-round pick has appeared in 14 games and has 14 total touchdowns, a 21% off-target rate and a 60% completion percentage to show for it. Penix has done well to avoid turnovers (six career INTs), but he's a nonfactor with his legs (career 28-81-2 rushing) and failed to post a single fantasy outing better than 10th last season. Penix tore an ACL in Week 11, which further complicates his path to beating out newcomer Tua Tagovailoa for the team's Week 1 starting gig. The 26-year-old might eventually emerge into a fine NFL starter, but even if he does, his lack of rushing will limit his fantasy output. He's well off the fantasy radar.

**Spin:**Making his first start of the season, McCarthy was efficient in getting the Giants into position to score, but all four of their touchdowns came on the ground -- including a one-yard plunge by the man he replaced under center, Jameis Winston, in the second quarter. McCarthy appeared in 10 games and totaled 11 passing TDs and 12 interceptions while completing an ugly 58% of his passes. McCarthy added some value with his legs (including four TDs), but his production was extremely inconsistent (18-plus fantasy points in four games, but 6.7 per game in his other six outings). The 23-year-old still has plenty of time to develop, but that will come as a backup to Kyler Murray this season. McCarthy is worth considering only in dynasty leagues.

Minnesota Vikings rookie kicker Will Reichard nailed a game-winning field goal as time expired to give his team its first preseason victory, but it was a different rookie who stole the show on Saturday.
Quarterback J.J. McCarthy, Minnesota's first-round pick in this year's draft, was the highly anticipated first-year player starring in Saturday's 24-23 win over the Las Vegas Raiders. After veteran Sam Darnold started the game, the rookie out of Michigan officially made his NFL debut late in the first quarter as he took the field for the Vikings' second drive.
Between the two teams, six quarterbacks attempted at least one pass in the game. McCarthy finished the game as the leader of them all in almost every statistical category: He had the most passing yards, passing touchdowns, pass attempts, completions, average yardage and the highest passer rating.
By the time the rookie gave way to third-string quarterback Jaren Hall late in the third quarter, he had solidified his strong first impression on an NFL stage.

**News:**4 days ago McCarthy completed 20 of 28 passes for 252 yards and no touchdowns or interceptions in Sunday's 27-21 overtime win over the Texans. He added one yard on his only carry.
texts.2:
**Spin:**Making his first start of the season, McCarthy was efficient in getting the Giants into position to score, but all four of their touchdowns came on the ground -- including a one-yard plunge by the man he replaced under center, Jameis Winston, in the second quarter. The victory alone was enough to keep McCarthy in the starting job, and after a bye he'll gear up for a Week 9 clash with the Eagles.
**ESPN Fantasy Projection:**McCarthy's career is off to a slow start after the 2024 first-round pick missed his entire rookie season because of an injury then struggled through 2025. McCarthy appeared in 10 games and totaled 11 passing TDs and 12 interceptions while completing an ugly 58% of his passes. McCarthy added some value with his legs (including four TDs), but his production was extremely inconsistent (18-plus fantasy points in four games, but 6.7 per game in his other six outings). The 23-year-old still has plenty of time to develop, but that will come as a backup to Kyler Murray this season. McCarthy is worth considering only in dynasty leagues.

Minnesota Vikings rookie kicker Will Reichard nailed a game-winning field goal as time expired to give his team its first preseason victory, but it was a different rookie who stole the show on Saturday.
Quarterback J.J. McCarthy, Minnesota's first-round pick in this year's draft, was the highly anticipated first-year player starring in Saturday's 24-23 win over the Las Vegas Raiders. After veteran Sam Darnold started the game, the rookie out of Michigan officially made his NFL debut late in the first quarter as he took the field for the Vikings' second drive.
Between the two teams, six quarterbacks attempted at least one pass in the game. McCarthy finished the game as the leader of them all in almost every statistical category: He had the most passing yards, passing touchdowns, pass attempts, completions, average yardage and the highest passer rating.
By the time the rookie gave way to third-string quarterback Jaren Hall late in the third quarter, he had solidified his strong first impression on an NFL stage.
